decision: took the skill list from Cory House's post and found an upstream for each skill
why: the post names no repos, so each pick is the best-licensed version, not proof of what he runs

decision: kept upstream captures out of git and committed only their provenance
why: several upstreams have no license and some text is Anthropic's
result: public repo carries no unlicensed text

decision: kept council, release-waves, autonomous-delivery and daily-log out; adapt agent-loop-spec and agent-loop-hygiene
why: the rest overlap pstack or need tools a hosted runner lacks

decision: made validation a separate stage with held-out tests the builder never sees
why: the software-factory reports say agents game tests they can edit

decision: land is deterministic code holding the only write token; the factory cannot edit workflows
why: the model must not hold publish rights or loosen its own gates

decision: first unit is a smoke test of model access from a hosted runner
why: riskiest unknown: the proxy lives on a private tailnet

decision: fixed the trust credential subject to GitHub's immutable format
why: token sub is repo:owner@id/repo@id, so the old pattern never matched

decision: added a masked path check after the token exchange passed but the model fetch failed
why: needed to tell DNS, policy and routing apart without leaking tailnet names

decision: switched the runner to a pre-signed ephemeral auth key
why: Tailnet Lock locks out runner devices joined through the trust credential

decision: smoke test passes end to end
why: unit 0 predicate: runner prints factory-smoke-ok

decision: scheduled the smoke test weekly
why: the auth key expires in 90 days and would otherwise fail silently

decision: accepted the package skeleton after reading the core and rerunning check
why: child summary alone is not proof

decision: widened forbidden paths from .github/workflows to all of .github
why: composite actions and CODEOWNERS steer gates without touching workflow files; the old test called CODEOWNERS ordinary

decision: validate must run the base branch's checks against the candidate
why: a patch could otherwise edit package.json scripts or delete tests to pass

decision: added opt-in human checkpoints before build and before merge, driven by a policy file under .github
why: owner wants a person to see some decisions; the factory must not be able to edit its own checkpoints

decision: accepted the Herdr-on-runner prototype after checking how it decides VERIFIED
why: it asserts on the host's subagent_result message and the child's own session, not on parent text

decision: moved the runtime to a controller on an exe.dev VM with checks in GitHub-hosted CI
why: owner choice; keeps model and Tailscale credentials out of GitHub and gives Linear its receiver

decision: copied Symphony's coordination layer: claims, reconcile tick, backoff, stall timeout, workspace invariants, WORKFLOW.md
why: proven shape for a tracker-driven daemon; no reason to invent our own

decision: kept three differences from Symphony: fixed stages, agent never writes to GitHub, automatic landing
why: no human reads the result, and the input is public issue text

decision: deleted the CI tailnet secrets, variables and the two tailnet workflows
why: owner revoked the Tailscale credential, key and signature; runners no longer need models
evidence: gh secret list empty, gh variable list empty

decision: v1 ends at Human Review; autonomy later through the checkpoint policy
why: owner choice

decision: use gh through exe.dev's GitHub integration and poll, instead of our own GitHub App and webhooks
why: owner wants plain gh; the integration keeps the token off the VM and polling removes public ingress

decision: created pi-factorio fresh, not cloned from dotfiles, with a repo-only GitHub integration acting as its bot
why: a factory box should inherit no personal integrations, and a bot author lets the owner approve its PRs

decision: proved gh reads, clones and writes from the VM with no token on it
why: labels are needed anyway, so creating them is the write test
evidence: gh label list --search factory: 4 labels; no ~/.config/gh on the VM

decision: models come from exe.dev's llm integration: Anthropic through the gateway, OpenAI through the ChatGPT subscription
why: owner chose option C; no model key on the VM and no tailnet

decision: provisioned the VM with a committed idempotent script
why: a script is the lever a reviewer can rerun

decision: pi -p answers from the VM on two Anthropic and two OpenAI models
why: unit 3 predicate; two families keep cross-family review possible

decision: default model on the VM is openai/gpt-6.1-sol; Anthropic waits for the owner's proxy
why: owner choice: the owner's Anthropic key lives in that proxy, and exe.dev credits are finite
evidence: pi -p with no --model answered default-ok on pi-factorio

decision: review seats are same-family and context-isolated until Anthropic is back
why: only one family is in use; disclosed rather than faked

decision: removed the factory-skeleton and factory-herdr-probe worktrees, branches kept
why: owner approved; both were merged

decision: wrote the v1 plan: 16 serial PRs, F04a to F13, all owner-merged under autopilot-stack
why: owner asked for a fully fleshed-out plan; pstack's multi-phase-plan playbook

decision: handed the project to a new session in herdr pane wQ:p1
why: owner is moving the whole setup to that session
